title: ATM screens and end-to-end flow
idea: The ATM frontend is a set of touchscreen screens driven by one reducer, so a double press or a network retry can never request cash twice.
points: Screens: insert card, PIN, amount, processing, take cash; the reducer picks one.
Amount buttons disable while processing, and the reducer ignores a second press.
A lost reply keeps the key; the bank later reverses an unconfirmed PENDING debit.
Follow-ups: add deposits as a new flow, or many banks behind a network switch.

messages.label: withdraw(S-1, 250000, wd-2)
messages.note: The reducer moved to PROCESSING and made key wd-2. An effect starts the call.

messages.label: POST /withdrawals
messages.note: The key travels in the Idempotency-Key header. The body is validated by zod.

messages.label: lock account, debit
messages.note: One transaction locks the account row, checks funds and inserts a PENDING row.

messages.label: reply lost
messages.note: The reply is lost. The screen shows a retry message and keeps wd-2.

messages.label: POST again, wd-2
messages.note: The customer presses the same amount. The same key is sent.

messages.label: 200 TX-2 PENDING
messages.note: The key is known, so the first result returns. No second debit.

messages.label: dispense notes
messages.note: Approved: the screen shows take cash while the machine pushes notes out.

messages.label: POST .../TX-2/confirm
messages.note: Notes taken: TX-2 becomes COMPLETED. A jam would call reverse instead.

code.title: Screen reducer
code.caption: Pure screen logic. Run it, then change the retried amount to 100000 and predict the key.

walk.text: The whole screen state: which screen, the amount, the key, the last message.
The bank counts PIN tries; the screen only shows what is left.
A press outside AMOUNT is ignored. The key is reused only for the same amount.
A network error returns to AMOUNT and keeps the key for a safe retry.
A decline is final for that attempt, so the key is dropped.
Inactivity ends the session, but never while a request is in flight.
The run: wrong PIN, a decline, a double press, a lost reply and a retry.

code.title: AmountScreen component
code.caption: A React component that renders state and dispatches events. Not run here.

walk.text: The effect fires on entering PROCESSING and sends the reducer's key.
409 and other 4xx are final declines; only a lost reply or 5xx retries the key.
Messages use an alert region; a busy note is announced politely.
Buttons only dispatch events, and all disable while busy.

pitfalls: Disabling buttons is not enough; the reducer and the Idempotency-Key must stop repeats.
Reusing a key for a new amount replays the old one; issue a fresh key.
Interview follow-up: say what happens if power fails after debit but before dispense.

quiz.q: In the run, what key does the retry after NETWORK_ERROR use?
quiz.why: DECLINED dropped wd-1, so the next press made wd-2. NETWORK_ERROR keeps it, and the same amount reuses it.

takeaway: One reducer owns the screens; one key per amount makes retries safe.

starters: Where should the ATM store the key if it reboots mid-request?
